android.desc:
There are many clocks & agenda on the store, but this one is yours.

That’s the deal: I went totally wild with many ideas over years of private usage with the goal of being on time and focused. What you got here is only the best of these ideas. 

All of the ones I tried that did not help I dropped, and the many that helped, I perfected:

> Define your own sequences of ringing,  text-to-speech, audio memo replay, some text in silence to check you’re still awake, then some other tone, louder, or invoke an AI prompt to get information from the internet and then speak out what the AI answered.
> Keep these AI prompts and answers in a google sheet you own to keep track, not just log these but also your stats over time: how much you snoozed etc… 
> Provide a spoken summary of yesterday’s activity: are you snoozing more these days?
> Agenda options like alerts on set dates, or recurrences, eg. some reminder on the last Friday of each month… 
> Android desktop widgets: a list to see what’s coming up, and also a leftover-time widget with the classic disk & shrinking wedge, that comes in M, L, XL, XXL widget size. So unless you’re blind, you won’t be time-blind!
> Categories, with Emojis and colours you can choose to make the app as cheerful or serious -looking as you want it to be. 
> Plans, to record ideas that don’t have a set date/time yet.
> As everything (alerts, logs, etc) is synced to a google sheet you own, both ways, if you want to do more agenda-organisation there, even script your scheduling, then nothing's blocked there is zero walled-garden, your skill is the limit.
- Same for AI: I include both the option to invoke Gemini on your (also free-tier) Google AI Studio instance, and also the option to just input you personal LLM's address and authentication... We're amongst friends here.

Before release my goal was reached: it works for me. I’m finally releasing this because it’s so much better for me than any of the other apps there, it could also be so for you. If not: ideas welcome. 

One underlying question probably: many of these apps on the store pretend they will help you with ADHD... I don’t suffer from ADHD, also I do not have dandruff. So: I did gather a lot of experience and a lot of feedback to make the app just right, also from a few doctors. 

The verdict is, if you… 
> Hyperfocus on entering many alerts and plans instead of getting things done.
> Think you only need a few hours sleep each night.
> Expect help from an ap

quotes.text:
So I've made this [me+vibe+tests]-coded Android alarm app called Promptly, and as Gemini-CLI on the Google Pro subscription is getting google-killed on June 18th, I set up two branches, one for Antigravity+Gemini3.5 and one for Pi-coding-agent with Qwen3-Coder-Next...

Running the same prompt on both with the same .md memory state...

Gemini3.5 is more "intelligent" but Antigravity gets it to decide to go on tangents that are quite time and token-consuming I think. Nice casino machine.

Pi+Qwen3 (~80GB, llama.cpp) is like vibecoding about 1.5 years ago, when you had to babysit, structure your program to have self-contained chunks, and keep an eye on all the cross-cutting concerns to not trip it up. When it works it works fine and when it fails it's my job to ensure it fails fast.

The code is about 10'000 lines of Kotlin in total so it already takes some effort to keep it simple for the AI. It's not a slopped quantity of code, i got solid feature creep :^)

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sixteenam.promptly ...hat tip to the recent copycat squatter btw it's an honor!
